'''Anna Catherine Gilbert''' (born 1972)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000049929161 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-11-27.</ref> is an American mathematician who works as the John C. Malone Professor of Statistics & Data Science, Applied Mathematics, and Electrical Engineering at [[Yale University]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://statistics.yale.edu/people|title=People|publisher=Yale University Department of Statistics & Data Science|access-date=2024-11-19}}</ref> She was previously a professor at the University of Michigan. Her research expertise is in [[randomized algorithm]]s for [[harmonic analysis]], [[image processing]], [[signal processing]], and large data sets.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.math.lsa.umich.edu/~annacg/vita/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Anna C. Gilbert|date=July 15, 2012|access-date=2015-10-11}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Gilbert earned a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1993, and completed her Ph.D. in 1997 from [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Ingrid Daubechies]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=24150}}</ref> After postdoctoral research at [[Yale University]], she joined [[AT&T Labs]], and continued there as a staff member until 2004, when she moved to Michigan.<ref name="cv"/>

==Research==
Gilbert's research discoveries have included the existence of [[Multifractal system|multifractal]] behavior in [[Transmission Control Protocol|TCP]]-based internet traffic,<ref>{{citation|first=Barry|last=Cipra|author-link=Barry Arthur Cipra|title=Oh, What a Tangled Web We've Woven....|journal=SIAM News|volume=33|issue=2|year=1999|url=https://archive.siam.org/pdf/news/624.pdf}}.</ref> the development of [[streaming algorithm]]s based on random projections for aggregating information from large data streams using very small amounts of working memory,<ref>{{citation|title=Sublinear Computing: When Ignorance Is Bliss|first=Barry|last=Cipra|journal=SIAM News|volume=37|issue=3|date=April 2004|url=https://archive.siam.org/pdf/news/90.pdf}}.</ref> and a foundational analysis of the ability of orthogonal [[matching pursuit]] to recover sparse signals with her student [[Joel Tropp]].

==Recognition==
She became a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Fellow]] in 2006.<ref name="cv"/> In addition to that, she won the NSF (National Science Foundation) Career award in 2006 (12). In 2008, she was awarded the [[NAS Award for Initiatives in Research]]  and the [[Association for Computing Machinery Douglas Engelbart Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://annacgilbert.github.io/cv/|title=Anna C. Gilbert|website=Anna C. Gilbert|language=en|access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> She also won the Signal Processing Best Paper award alongside Martin Strauss and Joel Tropp in 2010 from the European Association for Signal Processing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=U-M researchers win 2010 Signal Processing Best Paper Award |url=https://ece.engin.umich.edu/stories/u-m-researchers-win-2010-signal-processing-best-paper-award |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Electrical and Computer Engineering |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2013 she won the Ralph E. Kleinman Prize of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for her creative and deep contributions to the mathematics of signal processing, data analysis and communications".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/2013_luncheon.php|title=2013 Prizes and Awards Luncheon|work=SIAM Annual Meeting|date=July 9, 2013|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|access-date=2015-10-11}}.</ref> She was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014, speaking on "Mathematics in Science and Technology".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2015-10-01|archive-date=November 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She gave the von Neumann Lecture at the 2022 [[Joint Mathematics Meetings|Joint Mathematics Meeting]], titled "Metric representations: Algorithms and Geometry."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meetings (JMM) |first=Joint Mathematics |title=Joint Mathematics Meetings |url=https://www.jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2022/2268_invspeakers#driessche |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=Joint Mathematics Meetings |language=en}}</ref>
